more_info.overview: Talc is a naturally occurring hydrated magnesium silicate; the food-grade specification requires the material to be free of asbestos. Its anti-caking role is to reduce the tendency of particles in a food powder to stick together. A naturally occurring hydrated magnesium silicate mineral. Food-grade talc is required to be free of asbestos. The specified material is supplied as white powder. The specification describes it as effectively insoluble in water.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain chewing gum; meat preparations as defined by Regulation No 853/2004; non-heat–treated meat products; whole, broken, or flaked grain; dairy analogues, including beverage whiteners; vegetable oil pan spray.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.origin: A naturally occurring hydrated magnesium silicate mineral. Food-grade talc is required to be free of asbestos.
more_info.side_effects:
EFSA could not assess food-use safety because the toxicology data were insufficient in 2018.
The former shared silicate intake limit was considered obsolete.
